text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today as oil markets stabilized after a volatile week driven by Middle East tensions. Crude oil prices retreated on Friday following comments from Trump suggesting Iran conflict could end soon after midterm elections—reducing immediate geopolitical risk—but the stock has still gained 6% over two weeks as oil prices surged above $100 a barrel on supply disruptions from Saudi pipeline attacks and broader regional escalation.

The company sits at the intersection of competing forces: near-term relief from political deescalation talk is capping gains, but the underlying fundamentals remain supportive with U.S. crude at $97 and global prices at $109, well above levels that typically pressure refiner and producer margins.
